metaheuristic.definition: a general recipe for searching for the minimum of a function by sampling and updating a set of candidate points, used when the function gives no gradient or has many local minima
metaheuristic.excludes: exact methods that come with a proof of finding the minimum

bio-label.definition: an optimiser whose published description is framed by an animal, plant or other organism, here slime mould, grey wolf, particle swarm, bee colony, ant colony and invasive weed
bio-label.excludes: any claim that the method works the way the organism does

benchmark-function.definition: a formula with a known minimum, chosen to be easy or hard in a known way, on which optimisers are compared by how close they get
benchmark-function.excludes: real engineering problems, whose minimum is unknown

cma-es.field: evolutionary computation, after Hansen and colleagues
cma-es.definition: covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy: it samples candidates from a multivariate normal distribution and adapts the distribution's centre, shape and step size from the best samples
cma-es.excludes: the larger-population restart schedule known as IPOP, which our version did not use

search-box.definition: the allowed region, here every coordinate between -100 and 100; a method may only propose and keep points inside it
search-box.excludes: constraints other than simple bounds on each coordinate

centre-bias.definition: a tendency of a method's update rule to pull candidates toward the centre of the search box, which helps on any function whose minimum happens to sit there
centre-bias.excludes: good performance that survives when the minimum is moved

shifted-arm.definition: the version of each test function whose minimum is moved to a random point with every coordinate between -70 and 70 and whose axes are turned by a random rotation, the same for every method within one repeat
shifted-arm.excludes: the unshifted arm, with the minimum at the centre and the axes aligned

mean-rank.definition: each method's rank on each function by median final error, averaged over the seven functions; 1 is best and 10 is worst
mean-rank.excludes: how large the differences in error are

decade.definition: a factor of ten; a change of one decade in error is a change of one in its base-10 logarithm
decade.excludes: a difference on a linear scale

shift-penalty.definition: for one method, the median over the seven functions of how many decades its median error grows when the function moves from the unshifted arm to the shifted arm
shift-penalty.excludes: effects of the rotation alone, which the design does not separate from the shift

label-permutation.definition: shuffling which method name goes with which rank within each function, 2,000 times, to see how large a gap between the two groups' mean ranks arises by chance
label-permutation.excludes: uncertainty from the random repeats of each run

no-free-lunch.field: optimisation theory, after Wolpert and Macready
no-free-lunch.definition: the result that, averaged over all possible functions, every search method that never revisits a point does equally well, so any advantage on one class of functions is paid for on another
no-free-lunch.excludes: claims about any one class of functions, such as the test functions here

kruskal-wallis.definition: a rank-based test of whether several groups of numbers come from the same distribution
kruskal-wallis.excludes: a test of which group is better

centre-cheat.definition: a dummy method that only samples points within a tiny distance of the centre of the box, so it solves any function whose minimum sits there and nothing else
